name: Priya Wagner

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a small community orchestra from the violin chair, make rehearsal recordings and teach advanced pupils at the arts centre. I have a master’s in music and can get a difficult section playing together, but the centre pays less than that skill usually earns.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What follows you home from the rehearsal room?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I love the moment the first violins stop racing the cellos. My partner works changing shifts at a grocery warehouse; we have two school-age children and a mortgage, with less than a month of expenses saved. There are few similar music posts nearby, so a cancelled rehearsal reaches our kitchen quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the players that a faster booking list helps, provided our paid rehearsal rate stays on the calendar. A computer cannot decide when the players at the back needs another run.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We are already tight, despite my senior chair and strong playing. One cancelled paid rehearsal and a short warehouse week could leave the mortgage payment short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would lead the scheduled orchestra rehearsals and teach my five arts-centre pupils this winter. I already use AI sometimes to tidy emails, but I check names and dates against the paper roster; if a rehearsal cancels, I would stop renting the separate practice room that week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the bills we have now. A mild AI outcome does not make our small reserve any larger.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much is in the reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It would not cover one full month of household expenses. I do not call it a cushion when a boiler repair could use it all.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the orchestra pay for a cancellation?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the contract says so. I would ask the organiser to write a half-fee cancellation term before next season.

say: I would keep the **paid rehearsal rate** visible on the calendar.
I would ask for a **half-fee cancellation term** next season.
think: Our **thin reserve** and variable warehouse shifts leave the mortgage exposed.
A senior **violin chair** does not turn cancelled rehearsals into income.
do: Lead **paid rehearsals** and teach five arts-centre pupils this winter.
Cancel **practice-room rent** when rehearsal pay disappears; request a written half-fee term next season.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the mortgage even under mild AI change.
S0.quote: One cancelled paid rehearsal and a short warehouse week could leave the mortgage payment short.
fieldNote: Her **senior skill** coexists with low musician pay and less than one month saved.
She checks occasional **AI email drafting** against the roster before sharing dates.

steps.text: Lead paid orchestra rehearsals and teach five arts-centre pupils this winter
Cancel separate practice-room rent if a paid rehearsal is cancelled
Request written half-fee cancellation term before next orchestra season

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the players that cheap rehearsal tracks and planning software could eat paid preparation hours. I would ask the musicians’ association for a minimum rehearsal fee and a rule against reusing our recordings without consent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The recordings bring roughly a quarter of my own pay, and the centre might buy fewer from me. We have no month of savings to make a long pay cut feel abstract.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would take our invoices to the association and ask for a shared recording clause. In the first year I would try the centre’s new AI score index, which marks rehearsal sections, only after its librarian teaches me, using a part I own without pupil names; I would check each suggested rehearsal mark against my own score and stop if a note changes or the file leaves the centre library.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed if that quarter of my pay disappears while the mortgage is due. I expect recording orders to fall, and I have begun waking early to count which fees are signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you upload a pupil’s playing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No child’s audio goes into this test. If the librarian cannot explain where the owned score stays, I would use my pencil index instead.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the association to put first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A paid preparation hour belongs on the invoice. I would ask the other section leaders to sign the same fee request so one person is not blamed.

I would argue that **paid preparation** belongs on the invoice.
think: My **rehearsal recordings** bring about a quarter of my pay.

do: Bring **invoices** to the association this month for common recording and preparation terms.
Test the **score index** after librarian teaching on my nameless owned part; check marks manually and stop on errors or leakage.
feel: I feel **alarmed** at expected recording cuts with a mortgage and almost no reserve.
S1.quote: A paid preparation hour belongs on the invoice.
fieldNote: She seeks **collective fees** because a senior chair cannot negotiate every reuse alone.
The **new AI index** needs librarian instruction, an owned nameless part, manual comparison and a library-boundary stop.

steps.text: Ask musicians’ association for recording consent and paid preparation terms this month

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the orchestra that thinking AGI in 2028 could produce rehearsal tracks overnight. Robots able to play our violin parts follow around 2031, but the recording invoice could vanish three years sooner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the recordings to end in 2028 and some paid preparation to be cut. My partner’s warehouse hours change, so losing a quarter of my pay could quickly leave the mortgage short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would request signed orchestra dates and list recording invoices with my partner. In the first year after 2028, if orders stop, I would ask the lender before arrears for a temporary plan with the full extra interest and fees in writing; I would seek an advertised school strings post only if it accepts my music master’s or any required licence I hold, its written net pay after travel and childcare beats the lost fees, and pickup is covered. I would keep orchestra and pupils until a written offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed about a likely gap in the mortgage money. A good audition does not pay the next mortgage instalment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a course before a school offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask whether the post actually requires a teaching licence first. I cannot pay tuition from a reserve smaller than one month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your partner cover an audition day?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We can trade one pickup if the warehouse rota is posted in time. A regular school role would need a workable pickup plan every week, not one favour.

say: I would separate **2028 recording AGI** from 2031 playing robots.
I would seek **signed orchestra dates** and a real school vacancy.
think: I expect **recording fees** to end and paid preparation to shrink.
Variable **warehouse pay** cannot reliably fill the mortgage gap.
do: Request **signed orchestra dates** and count invoices now; keep orchestra and pupils until a written school offer.
Request a **lender plan** before arrears if 2028 orders stop, with full extra interest and fees in writing.
Seek **posted school strings work** only if qualified, written net pay beats lost fees after travel/childcare and pickup works.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by a likely mortgage gap despite my skill.
S2.quote: A good audition does not pay the next mortgage instalment.
fieldNote: The likely **2028 recording loss** precedes playing robots around 2031.
A school move needs **actual eligibility**, posted work, written net replacement pay, pickup and a signed offer.

steps.text: Keep orchestra and five pupils until suitable written school offer is signed
Request lender plan before arrears if 2028 orders stop, with full written extra interest and fees
Seek qualifying posted school role if orders stop; written net-after-travel/childcare pay beats loss, pickup fits

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the orchestra that five years until AGI by 2031 lets us build a paid way to pass our craft on. Playing robots follow around 2034; they do not pay a teacher for preparation today.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The recordings could still disappear by 2031. A separate Saturday ensemble class might replace some of those fees, but I cannot front a hall deposit from the mortgage account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I would ask the independent civic hall for a free Saturday room after our children’s sports pickup. I would start a six-week ensemble class only if seven adults prepay enough to cover my teaching and preparation and the hall confirms safe shared instruments; in the first year after 2031 I would repeat it only while seven still prepay my time, the free room and safe instruments remain available, and pickup fits. I would keep paid orchestra work meanwhile.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious until the class pays for my time. Five years before AGI lets me test a paid ensemble class without risking our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes the shared instruments safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The hall must inspect each loan instrument before the first class. If it cannot, adults must bring instruments in good working order or I will cancel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if only four adults prepay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Four fees do not cover preparation and teaching. I would refund them rather than run an unpaid group.

I would refuse a **hall deposit** from our mortgage money.
think: My **recording fees** may end by 2031 before 2034 playing robots.

Renew the **paid class** after 2031 only with seven prepayments covering my time, available free room, safe instruments and pickup.
Keep **paid orchestra work** while its rehearsals continue.
feel: I feel **anxious** until the independent class pays my preparation and teaching.
S3.quote: Five years before AGI lets me test a paid ensemble class without risking our mortgage.
fieldNote: The class is a **separate income source** with seven prepayments covering both teaching and preparation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children that a decade until AGI by 2036 is time to learn a skill and ask what it pays. Robots who can play violin arrive around 2039, not in the same year as the recording software.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may still lead the orchestra at 53, but the mortgage needs money in 2026. The recordings could go before a robot picks up a bow, and our small reserve means we must act now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would use any extra cleared recording fee after food and mortgage to build one month of household savings. Over the decade I would run the independent class only with seven prepayments covering my teaching and preparation, a free room, safe instruments and pickup; in the first year after 2036 I would seek a posted school strings role only if orchestra pay falls, the school accepts my qualifications, written net pay after travel and childcare replaces lost fees and pickup works. I would keep the paid orchestra and pupils until a written offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stay anxious about the household bills even with a decade to plan. A calendar cannot stand in for one month of savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you save a promised recording fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after it clears and food and mortgage are paid. If no extra fee arrives, I cannot move a number into the savings account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave the orchestra for a school title?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a posted paid job with written hours and enough net pay. I would not give up signed rehearsals for an interview.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because recording fees could disappear before I find a school post, and our savings would not cover one mortgage month. Signed orchestra dates, a costed lender plan and an actual eligible school vacancy with net pay that covers pickup would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who pays for the pencil marks I make before anyone else arrives. The first violin note is heard by the audience, but the unpaid preparation begins at home.

headlineQuote: The first violin note is heard by the audience, but the unpaid preparation begins at home.
portrait: At **43**, Priya leads a community orchestra, teaches five pupils and records rehearsal parts with a music master’s and strong skill.
Her **lower pay**, changing partner shifts, mortgage, two children and less than one month saved keep ordinary cancellations serious.
She uses **AI occasionally** for emails and tests a score index only with librarian instruction, owned parts and manual checks.
She seeks **collective recording terms** and tries a separately paid ensemble class only with seven prepayments and safe, free space.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase recording fees before an eligible paid school opening appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed orchestra dates**, a costed lender plan and a posted qualified school job with workable net pay and pickup would help.
